about: Every difference between the AArch64 kernels (QEMU and handset) (kernel/sel4/aarch64/build.py) and upstream seL4. Same rules as kernel/sel4/delta.json; a source hash written as "shared" is the one recorded there. After a deliberate change run python3 kernel/sel4/aarch64/build.py --update.

nearest_verified.why: No verified configuration matches. The nearest is AARCH64_imx8mm_verified: the same architecture, core (Cortex-A53) and interrupt controller family. The build's CMakeCache.txt must differ from it in exactly these options, the 'beyond' ones (which it leaves at upstream's default), the compiler and the source changes above.

KernelPlatform.proof: Another platform: none of the proof's platform assumptions were checked for it.

KernelVerificationBuild.proof: The build is not restricted to what the proofs cover.

KernelArmHypervisorSupport.proof: The verified AArch64 configurations run the kernel at EL2; this one runs at EL1, a configuration with no proof.

KernelAllowSMCCalls.proof: Upstream's general SMC forwarding is off. The handset kernel instead has the ellis Wi-Fi extension (four fixed secure-monitor calls behind one root cap, ellis-wifi.patch); the QEMU kernel makes no SMC (the build checks).

KernelMaxNumBootinfoUntypedCaps.proof: A larger boot information array; the proofs are parametric in it, but this value was not checked.

KernelNumDomains.proof: The proofs are set up to be robust to this number (upstream CAVEATS.md); no domain scheduling is used.

src/arch/arm/64/traps.S.why: svc #0 (the Linux AArch64 system call instruction) is dispatched on x8, so a Linux call is always an unknown-syscall fault for the thread's fault handler whatever x7 holds; an x8 outside 0..2^31-1 is reported as 0x10000, so no x8 selects one of seL4's own (negative) numbers either. Native seL4 calls use svc #1.

libsel4/sel4_arch_include/aarch64/sel4/s.why: libsel4's seven system call stubs issue svc #1 to match.

src/arch/arm/machine/gic_v3.c.why: On ellis the redistributor region is one 128 KiB frame per booted core instead of a fixed 1 MiB.

tools/hardware.yml.why: Adds the violet,ellis-boot-gic device rule: the kernel maps the distributor and four redistributor frames.

include/arch/arm/arch/64/mode/object/str.why: Adds ellis_wifi_cap (arch cap tag 29) on the ellis platform.
The ellis_wifi_cap has no size, object or region, like the ASID control cap.

src/arch/arm/kernel/boot.c.why: Puts the ellis_wifi_cap in the root task's seL4_CapSMC slot (the slot upstream's SMC cap would use; KernelAllowSMCCalls stays OFF).

src/arch/arm/64/object/objecttype.c.why: Derivation gives a null cap (no copies), and an invocation goes to ellisWifiInvocation (invoke.h).

src/plat/ellis/config.cmake.why: The ellis platform as an AArch64 kernel on Cortex-A53 with GICv3 and the ARM generic timer: QEMU virt's 62.5 MHz timer, or the handset's 13 MHz with VioletHandsetBoard. Not an upstream platform.

src/plat/ellis/kernel-overlay.dts.why: Device tree overlay: the kernel's GIC node and reserved memory.

src/plat/ellis/moto-radio-memory.dts.why: The handset's connectivity memory reservations, so the 64-bit kernel sees the same memory map.

src/plat/ellis/factory-base.dts.why: The base device tree: qemu.dts for QEMU; for the handset, the tree decompiled from the factory boot image at build time (not in this repository), as the 32-bit handset kernel's.

handset.how: For the handset, kernel/sel4/aarch64/build.py decompiles the base device tree from the factory boot image with dtc. The build stops unless that image has this SHA-256.

src/plat/ellis/wifi/monitor.S.why: Four secure-monitor call stubs with fixed MediaTek SiP function IDs, in A64. Assembled for the handset only.

include/arch/arm/arch/object/ellis_wifi/.why: ellisWifiInvocation, the 32-bit kernel's: one of four permitted requests becomes one secure-monitor call with fixed arguments. On QEMU the stubs are C functions that fail.
The four permitted operations and their fixed monitor arguments, the 32-bit kernel's.

CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE.value: upstream's llvm.cmake, in the prepared tree
CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE.why: The toolchain file seL4 ships for clang.

TRIPLE.why: The clang target triple llvm.cmake uses.

PYTHON3.why: The interpreter for the kernel's code generators.

KernelPlatform.why: The VioletOS board port; no upstream platform, so no upstream proof configuration.

KernelArmExportVCNTUser.why: User level reads the virtual counter.

KernelArmExportPTMRUser.why: No user thread may program the EL0 physical timer: the kernel does not switch it between threads, so any app could cancel or move another thread's wake-up.

KernelArmHypervisorSupport.why: The kernel runs at EL1; QEMU virt without virtualization starts there.

KernelRootCNodeSizeBits.why: The supervisor's root CNode: on AArch64 its device windows, scanout and camera are mapped as 4 KiB frames (no 64 KiB or 1 MiB pages), about 6000 capabilities on QEMU, beyond the default 4096 slots.

VioletHandsetBoard.value: ON for the handset, OFF for QEMU
VioletHandsetBoard.why: Selects the handset's 13 MHz timer instead of QEMU virt's 62.5 MHz (src/plat/ellis/config.cmake).

smc.why: The only SMC instructions in the AArch64 kernels: the stubs in monitor.S, handset only. The QEMU kernel has none (the build checks both).
